newsitem.title: USA: Shell Ill. refinery fire caused toxic emission-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Shell Ill. refinery fire caused toxic emission-EPA.

text.p: A fire at Shell Oil Co's Wood River, Illinois refinery on Tuesday caused an emission of toxic sulphur dioxide, though the manner of the release meant there was no threat to the local community, according to Environmental Protection Agency officials.
The fire broke out at the plant's gas furnace unit where volatile compounds, such as propane and butane, are processed, according to Illinois EPA field officer Steve Farrand.

The 500 pounds of sulphur dioxide was "above the reportable quantity, which is a medium-large release, but it was a through-air release. There was no evacuation and there is no health threat," Farrand said.
Shell is conducting an investigation into the cause of the incident which would take "days at least, possibly weeks," said Farrand.

The gas unit directly affected by the fire will remain down until the investigation is completed, though the alkylation unit taken down as a consequence of a lack of olefin feedstocks is expected to be restarted on Wednesday, a Shell offical said.
The Shell plant has a rated capacity to process 280,000 barrels a day of crude oil.

The Shell spokeswoman said the plant's environmental officers said that the sulphur dioxide was above EPA reportable levels but low enough that personell at the plant weren't evacuated. The plant is sorrounded by five populated areas but the release "posed no community threat," she said.
The plant is owned by Shell Oil Co, the U.S. unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group Royal Dutch Shell Transport and Trading.
